transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you. Um… I guess what brings me in is that lately I feel like I can’t really settle in my own body. It’s probably not as dramatic as that sounds, but when I’m supposed to sit quietly and do paperwork or talk through household plans with someone, I get this restless feeling like I just can’t stay still or stay with it. I’m not sure if that’s the right way to explain it.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in a constant way, at least. I mean, I worry about normal things, like if I’m forgetting something or if I’ve handled something the right way, but I wouldn’t say I’m just anxious for no reason all the time. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.
When you’re doing something that needs sustained focus, do you often find your attention drifting even when you want to stay on it?

Yes… I think so. I don’t mean to be difficult about it, but I’ll sit down with something like a planning email or even a chapter of a book, and I start out really intending to focus. Then a few minutes later I realize I’m just looking at the same paragraph again and again, and none of it has actually gone in. 

It’s not every single second, but it happens enough that I notice it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Thinking back to when you were a child, did you already have trouble paying attention?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible student or anything, because I wasn’t trying to be difficult, but looking back it was kind of already there in elementary school.

I was the kid with the messy desk, and I’d forget permission slips or not bring things home when I was supposed to. Teachers would sometimes write notes that I was talking when I shouldn’t, or that I seemed like I couldn’t stay in my seat. At the time I think it was just treated like I needed to try harder or be more polite, which… maybe I did, but it does feel like it was a pattern. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you ever had a period when your mood was unusually high, euphoric, or unusually irritable for you?

I don’t think so… not like unusually high or euphoric. I can get irritable sometimes, probably more than I’d like to admit, but it feels tied to stress or being overwhelmed, not like a whole separate period where I’m a different person.

I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, though.
Do these attention and restlessness problems cause significant trouble for you at work, school, or at home?

Yes… unfortunately, yes. I mean, I try really hard to be dependable, and I don’t want to sound like I’m just making excuses, but it has caused problems.

At home and with volunteering things, people can’t always count on me the way they should be able to. I’ll mean to follow through, and then something gets missed or I’m late getting something done, and it affects other people. I’ve actually had to step back from some responsibilities because I kept letting things fall through, even when I really cared about them.

That’s probably the part I feel worst about. Is that the kind of trouble you mean?
Do these attention and restlessness problems show up in more than one part of your life?

Yes, I think so. It’s not just one setting.

At home it comes up, and also in the volunteer things I’ve been involved with. I hate saying that, because I do try really hard, but people can’t always count on me the way I want them to. I’ll drop the ball or not follow through the way I meant to, and eventually I’ve had to step back from some responsibilities because it wasn’t fair to everyone else.

So… yes, more than one area. Does that make sense?
When you feel restless, is it usually because your mind is caught up in worry?

Sometimes worry is part of it, but… I don’t think it’s only that.

What really brings me in is more this feeling like I can’t settle in my own body anymore, especially when I’m supposed to sit quietly and do paperwork or talk through household plans with someone. I feel like I should be able to just sit and handle it like an adult, but I get this restless, unsettled feeling.

I don’t know if that answers it exactly. It’s not always a specific worry in my head. It’s more like I just can’t get comfortable staying still with the task.
Do you often interrupt people before they’ve finished speaking?

Yes… I’m embarrassed to say I do sometimes.

I really do care about being respectful, and I don’t mean to cut people off, but especially with my husband I’ll jump in before he’s finished, or I’ll finish what I think someone is about to say. It’s like the response is there and it comes out before I’ve made myself wait.

I usually realize it right after and feel bad. I’m not trying to be rude, but… yes, that does happen.
Did these attention and restlessness problems get noticeably worse after a particular stressful event?

Not exactly after something stressful, no… or at least I don’t think of it that way.

It’s been more noticeable since I got married and our routines sort of merged together. That was about a year and five months ago. I don’t want to make it sound like marriage caused it or anything — it’s just that sharing routines and responsibilities made the problems harder to hide, I guess.

Is that the kind of timing you mean?
When you feel that restless, unsettled sensation, does getting up and moving around make it feel better?

Yes, usually it does help a little… or at least it feels like a relief to be able to move.

It’s not that I’m trying to avoid things, exactly. It’s more like when I’m supposed to sit quietly and do paperwork, or go over household plans, I start feeling like I can’t settle in my own body. If I get up, walk around, shift positions, get a drink of water—something like that—it can take the edge off.

I don’t know if that’s what you mean, but sitting still through it is the hard part.
When you start worrying about things, do you find it hard to stop or control the worrying?

I’m not totally sure. I do worry about things sometimes, of course, but I don’t know that I’d say it’s uncontrollable exactly.

Usually I can talk myself down or distract myself after a while. Maybe it depends on the situation. I don’t want to overstate it—when you say “hard to control,” do you mean like it keeps going no matter what I try?
Are you able to focus much better when you’re doing something that’s genuinely interesting to you?

Yes… I think so. If it’s something I’m genuinely interested in, it’s easier to stay with it.

With things that are less engaging, even if I mean to focus, I can start out fine—like with a planning email or a chapter of a book—and then a few minutes later I realize I’m just staring at the same paragraph and none of it actually went in. It’s a little embarrassing, because I am trying. Does that make sense?
